section_summary: This section completes a translated law establishing the Japan Electric Generation and Transmission Company and includes related 1938 laws governing debentures and the electric industry. Embassy despatches then report the organization of electric power control bodies, the ordinances putting the laws into effect, and the facilities designated for transfer to the new company.

subfiles.title: Japan Electric Generation and Transmission Company Limited Law
subfiles.about: Completes the law establishing and regulating the Japan Electric Generation and Transmission Company.
subfiles.summary: The remaining articles cover compensation and succession of rights, company officers and business duties, financing privileges, government subsidies, and supervision. They also establish penalties and procedures for organizing the company.

subfiles.title: Law No. 78: Disposition of Debentures in Connection with the Control of Electric Power
subfiles.about: Regulates debentures secured by electric facilities transferred to the new company.
subfiles.summary: The law provides for collateral deposits, assumption or guarantee of debenture payments, and purchase of remaining facilities in a factory syndicate. It addresses investors’ claims and the treatment of existing security arrangements.

subfiles.title: Law No. 79: Revision of the Electric Industry Law
subfiles.about: Revises ministerial powers over electric enterprises and aligns the industry law with the new company law.
subfiles.summary: The amendments address oversight of depreciation and supply, transmission on request, and ordered transfers of electric enterprises. Extracts from the earlier Electric Industry Law supply context.

subfiles.title: Division of Far Eastern Affairs note on Tokyo despatch No. 3037
subfiles.about: Notes the Embassy’s translations and press clipping on electric power control.
subfiles.summary: Flags the enclosed organizational documents and reported transfer estimates for departmental use.

subfiles.title: Despatch No. 3037: Government Control of the Electric Industry
subfiles.from: Joseph C. Grew, American Embassy, Tokyo
subfiles.about: Forwards documents on Japan’s electric power control bodies and reports plans for transferring generating facilities.
subfiles.summary: Grew describes the new deliberative commission, its first meeting, and press estimates that the planned company would control about 85 percent of thermal and 60 percent of hydraulic generating plants. He encloses ordinances, a press clipping, and a membership list.

subfiles.title: Imperial Ordinance No. 369: Electric Power Deliberative Commission
subfiles.about: Establishes the commission’s remit, membership, and administration.
subfiles.summary: The commission will advise on controlled generation, transmission, and rates, with the Minister of Communications as chairman.

subfiles.title: Japan Times clipping: ¥780,000,000 of Assets Decided for Investment in Projected Power Firm
subfiles.about: Reports the commission’s proposed scale and criteria for asset transfers.
subfiles.summary: Reports a proposed ¥780 million investment of existing companies’ assets in the new power company.

subfiles.title: Imperial Ordinance No. 368: Revision of the Electric Committee’s Organization
subfiles.about: Revises the Electric Committee’s advisory responsibilities under the Electric Industry Law.
subfiles.summary: Updates the committee’s remit and reproduces relevant provisions of its 1932 organization ordinance.

subfiles.title: Imperial Ordinance No. 320: Preparatory Bureau for Electric Power Control
subfiles.about: Defines the bureau responsible for preparing government control of electric power.
subfiles.summary: Sets out the bureau’s supervision, staffing, councillors, and duties.

subfiles.title: Members of the Electric Power Deliberative Commission
subfiles.about: Lists regular and special commission members and secretaries.
subfiles.summary: Names commission members, special members, and secretaries with selected official posts.

subfiles.title: Division of Far Eastern Affairs note on Tokyo despatch No. 3206
subfiles.about: Assesses the Embassy’s translations of electric power control ordinances.
subfiles.summary: States that the despatch need not be read but its translations may be useful for the files.

subfiles.title: Despatch No. 3206: Government Control of the Electric Industry
subfiles.from: Joseph C. Grew, American Embassy, Tokyo
subfiles.about: Forwards six implementing ordinances and a summary of facilities ordered transferred to the new company.
subfiles.summary: Grew reports the designated transfer of about 7,100 kilometres of transmission lines, roughly 79 percent of thermal generating capacity, and associated transformers. He discusses the effects on major companies, valuation difficulties, and press reports of an April 1939 launch.

subfiles.title: Imperial Ordinance No. 574: Enforcement Date for Part of the Electric Power Control Law
subfiles.about: Makes Articles 1 and 2 of the Electric Power Control Law effective on August 10, 1938.
subfiles.summary: Sets the enforcement date and reproduces the affected articles.

subfiles.title: Imperial Ordinance No. 575: Enforcement of the Electric Power Control Law
subfiles.about: Defines the generating, transmission, and transforming facilities subject to electric power control.
subfiles.summary: The ordinance specifies capacity and voltage thresholds for facilities under the new company’s control. It provides exceptions, including for existing or under-construction hydraulic plants above 5,000 kilowatts.

subfiles.title: Imperial Ordinance No. 576: Application Date of the Company Law
subfiles.about: Sets August 10, 1938, as the enforcement date of the company law.
subfiles.summary: Brings the Japan Electric Generation and Transmission Company Limited Law into force.

subfiles.title: Imperial Ordinance No. 577: Enforcement of the Company Law
subfiles.about: Specifies procedures for share purchases, debentures, registrations, and ministerial consultations.
subfiles.summary: The ordinance details applications to sell shares, payment with debentures, approval and valuation of debenture issues, and registration. It also governs consultation over public facilities, water use, construction orders, and compensation.

subfiles.title: Imperial Ordinance No. 578: Enforcement Date of Law No. 78
subfiles.about: Sets August 10, 1938, as the enforcement date of the debentures law.
subfiles.summary: Brings Law No. 78 of 1938 into force.

subfiles.title: Imperial Ordinance No. 579: Application of the Debentures Law
subfiles.about: Sets procedures for collateral, assumption of debenture liabilities, purchases, and payment guarantees.
subfiles.summary: The ordinance defines acceptable collateral and its valuation, then describes agreements and notices when the new company assumes debenture obligations. It provides for settlement of price or exchange losses, purchase of remaining facilities, company or government guarantees, and ministerial consultation.

subfiles.title: Electric Power and Allied Facilities to Be Transferred as Investment
subfiles.from: Official Gazette; forwarded by the American Embassy, Tokyo
subfiles.about: Summarizes facilities designated for transfer to the Japan Electric Generation and Transmission Company.
subfiles.summary: The schedule lists owners and counts of transmission lines by voltage, transforming plants, and generating plants. It includes private utilities, railway companies, prefectures, and the cities of Osaka and Kobe.
